scope: Only two exact persistence-and-process correlations. Keep original warning findings and inspect every byte and sibling normally. No package, advisory, native-code, installation or execution approval.
evidence: Static in-memory inspection of the existing cached libdbus-sys 0.2.7 crate, SHA-256 verified against the desktop app's reviewed Cargo.lock. No download, extraction to disk or target execution.

reviews.reason: The only persistence-regex match is launchctl at line 4340 in _dbus_lookup_launchd_socket. Its fixed argument is getenv (4342), followed by the requested environment-variable name (4344); _read_subprocess_line_argv returns the existing socket path. It does not load/bootstrap/enable a job or write a LaunchAgent. The process regex matches subprocess in comments at 3907/3914. This file does have real fork/exec support: _dbus_connect_exec (1033-1105), the bounded subprocess reader (3926-4051), and optional X11 dbus-launch autolaunch (4138 onward). Those capabilities and PATH lookup are not denied or authorized by this finding-specific review. The inspected persistence/process co-occurrence is not evidence of installing persistence.
reviews.publisher: David Henningsson; bundled D-Bus upstream source

reviews.reason: The only persistence-regex match is the documented command launchctl getenv DBUS_LAUNCHD_SESSION_BUS_SOCKET at line 3747. Process matches are the transport-description prose at 3623 and unixexec address documentation at 4058. The launchd section explains reading an existing per-user socket; the unixexec section describes real process-transport arguments, not executed XML. No blanket XML/documentation exclusion is added: only these exact original bytes and this rule receive a retained warning instead of a blocking correlation. Strong findings, changed content and every other archive member remain subject to normal inspection.

limitations: This is a review of two regex correlations, not a complete D-Bus vulnerability audit or proof of safe execution.
